bestBets.overview: Wodonga was rated Heavy 8 at lunchtime on Saturday (34mm of rain for the previous 7 days) but the forecast though the weekend and early in the week is all rather delightful and we should see a sunny low 20s on raceday so there is room for plenty of improvement. Just perfect for the first day of spring in fact. We're off and running with a 2050m Maiden. MARANOA BOY has had four starts, all on Heavy ground. Rolled forward last start and to good effect but the only horse that settled in front of him (the $2.60 fave) won it. He should be nicely poised in running here as well. KING KAUFFO not so much; he could even be back last. Both he and GOOD LORDY ME are ready to step out to a distance they will appreciate.

raceTips.comment: The prospect of an improving track could be beneficial for Good Lordy Me. He didn't seem comfortably on a very heavy surface and his performance was excusable given he was caught wide on a day that suited those who settle on the rail. He was narrowly beaten on dry ground in two 2000m maidens last campaign and should be fit enough now third-up to press forward and lead. Maranoa Boy looked to have the race won at Murtoa before being narrowly beaten late by Sea Danger. All his racing has been on heavy ground and he may appreciate a firmer surface.

bestBets.overview: 5 and 14 ran on Sunday so presumably miss. BOLD JESTER has a draw to set him up comfortably in the front half and he has been solid in defeat so far on both wet and dry. Came from the back and was no threat to the leader at Mildura and in fact the leaders also won at Mildura and Wangaratta prior. Some of the on-pace runners here - SCORCHING BEAUTY and GALAGACISCO - look the main stumbling blocks here as well. Lone newcomer MODERN ROYAL has been OK in two jumpouts (April and August) so would look at her with a touch of respect.

raceTips.comment: Bold Jester has a golden opportunity to finally win his maiden. It is not a deep race to begin with, and Handsome Missile is likely to be scratched given he raced at Echuca on Sunday. Bold Jester's run was much better than it looks at Murtoa due to the severe rails in run bias. He was buried back in the pack and the winner Whimsy Smile scooted along in the lead. Scorching Beauty knocked up after leading at Geelong and was comfortably beaten by Shah Jahan. The form out of the race has proven to be strong and she now has the blinkers going on. Galagacisco maps to settle near the lead from barrier one and that often is a good position to be at Wodonga.

bestBets.overview: Two likely leaders in this one and frankly they look to be the two best winning chances in the race. BRUTIFY was successful here two back and has been good all through the current prep in fact. We know all about Chelsea Thompson's amazing record for the stable - it's now 8 from 19 overall - and it can continue here. MORE HIGHS ON ME was runner-up to BRUTIFY here on July 26 (meets her 2 kilos better for a 2L margin) and has backed up with a nostril defeat a fortnight ago. Clearly poses a threat here. LORD DOMINO off Heavy and rising from 1100 to 1300m should not be forgotten about.

raceTips.comment: Kowhai is an attractive price in early markets at $8.50. She has previously struggled fresh at 1200m, so not too concerned about the first-up effort on a sticky track at Wangaratta. She found the line well enough and should now be better suited rising in distance on a drying track. She maps to trail the speed and should hopefully finish over the top late. Brutify scored an easy win at this track and distance two starts back and backed up that run with another solid effort at Wangaratta last start. She is very genuine, maps to lead and will be tough to run down. More Highs On Me was two lengths off Brutify when they met last start and has since run well behind Hughie. She too is hard to knock on form and is ideally placed on her home track.

She will fight for favouritism with LIGHTNING FLASH whose recent efforts clearly demonstrate she is a big winning chance. HARRY CAVIAR and PHANTOM'S CHASE (favourite last start in very similar company) end up lightest raced of the group and their best has them in the finish

raceTips.comment: Whistle Down is extremely well graded in a BM56 if she can bounce back to anywhere near her best form. She was a consistent city performer when previously trained by Symon Wilde but concede her form tapered off at the back end of her current preparation. Since changed stables and was basically given a trial in her first run for Reece Goodwin over 1600m at Pakenham last start. The track drying out is key to her chances and she can settle close to the lead up to this distance. Lightning Flash has won two of her past four and was narrowly denied on her home track last start. No reason why she shouldn't run well again, although her form seems to be better on really testing tracks.
